sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Gradient Boosting (model_id python-gradient-boosting) is a Python challenger model that predicts the target default.payment.next.month and is compared against the production default model; per the recorded business purpose (an inferred field), it informs but does not drive decisions. It is assigned risk tier 2. It uses the public UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records of credit-card clients in Taiwan, payment history April to September 2005), which is intended here as demonstration data only and is not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. The business owner and intended business use are not documented.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier with default hyperparameters except random_state set to a seed (default 42), trained on an inferred stratified 80/20 train/test split using the same seed. Preprocessing renames the target column, drops ID and rows with missing values, validates the dataset shape and default rate, casts the target to integer, and applies no feature scaling. Predictors are 21 inferred input features (LIMIT_BAL, EDUCATION, MARRIAGE, PAY_0 and PAY_2 to PAY_6, BILL_AMT1 to BILL_AMT6, PAY_AMT1 to PAY_AMT6), with ID, SEX and AGE excluded. An inferred decision threshold of 0.5 is applied.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: Default hyperparameters are used with no tuning or cross-validation shown, and no justification is documented; there is no class imbalance handling, and categorical fields such as EDUCATION, MARRIAGE and PAY_* are used as raw numeric values without encoding. The model assumes SEX and AGE are fairness-only attributes and an expected training default rate of about 22% (20-24%), but fairness evaluation results, validation metrics and prediction PSI are not available in the provided results. Performance metrics, acceptance criteria, the production data loader, decision threshold calibration, monitoring, retraining frequency and approval status are not documented. Several fields (business purpose, input features, train fraction and decision threshold) are inferred and should be confirmed.
